name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q01 - Definition of chemical bond and noble gases

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The attractive force which holds various constituents such as atoms or ions together in different chemical species is called a chemical bond.

Statement II: Noble gases, except helium which has a duplet, possess a stable valence shell configuration of eight electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A chemical bond is defined as the attractive force holding constituents (atoms, ions, etc.) together to form stable chemical species and molecules.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I accurately defines a chemical bond as the attractive force holding constituent atoms or ions together in a chemical species.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II accurately states that noble gases possess a closed-shell octet configuration of \(ns^2 np^6\) in their valence shell, with the exception of helium which has a complete duplet configuration of \(1s^2\).

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Both statements represent established fundamental concepts of chemical bonding and electronic stability.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q02 - Valence electrons and group valence in bonding

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the formation of a molecule, inner shell electrons actively participate in chemical combination while outer shell electrons remain unaffected.

Statement II: The group valence of an element is always calculated by adding 8 to the number of dots in its Lewis symbol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chemical combination involves only the outer shell electrons, known as valence electrons, while the inner shell electrons are well protected and do not generally take part in bonding.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is incorrect because it is the outer shell (valence) electrons that participate in chemical combination, not the inner shell electrons.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is incorrect because the group valence is generally either equal to the number of dots in the Lewis symbol or equal to \(8\) minus the number of dots, not \(8\) plus the number of dots.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Evaluating both definitions shows that both statements contradict the principles of valence and Lewis electron dot representations.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q03 - Comparison of sigma and pi orbital overlap

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A sigma (\(\sigma\)) bond is formed by the end-to-end or head-on overlap of bonding orbitals along the internuclear axis.

Statement II: A pi (\(\pi\)) bond is stronger than a sigma (\(\sigma\)) bond because the extent of sidewise orbital overlap is significantly greater.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A covalent bond formed by axial (head-on) overlap along the internuclear axis is a sigma bond, whereas a bond formed by lateral or sidewise overlap perpendicular to the internuclear axis is a pi bond.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is correct because end-to-end overlap of atomic orbitals along the internuclear axis forms a sigma bond.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is incorrect because the extent of lateral overlap in a pi bond is much smaller than the axial overlap in a sigma bond, which makes a pi bond weaker than a sigma bond, not stronger.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Comparing the two statements shows that the definition of a sigma bond is accurate, while the claim regarding pi bond strength and overlap extent is false.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Final Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q04 - Dipole moments of beryllium and boron fluorides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The net dipole moment of beryllium difluoride (\(\mathrm{BeF}_2\)) is large and non-zero due to the high electronegativity difference between beryllium and fluorine.

Statement II: In boron trifluoride (\(\mathrm{BF}_3\)), the vector sum of the three individual \(\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{F}\) bond dipole moments is zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The net dipole moment of a polyatomic molecule is the vector sum of its individual bond moments and depends on the molecular geometry.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is incorrect because beryllium difluoride (\(\mathrm{BeF}_2\)) is a linear molecule (\(180^\circ\) bond angle) in which the two equal \(\mathrm{Be}-\mathrm{F}\) bond dipole moments point in exactly opposite directions and cancel out completely, giving a net dipole moment of zero.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is correct because boron trifluoride (\(\mathrm{BF}_3\)) has a symmetrical trigonal planar geometry with \(120^\circ\) bond angles, so the resultant of any two bond dipoles is equal and opposite to the third bond dipole, yielding a vector sum of zero.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Statement I asserts a non-zero dipole moment for linear \(\mathrm{BeF}_2\), which is incorrect, whereas Statement II correctly explains the zero net dipole moment in symmetrical planar \(\mathrm{BF}_3\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q05 - Electron pair repulsion and water bond angle

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to VSEPR theory, the repulsive interaction of electron pairs decreases in the order: lone pair - lone pair > lone pair - bond pair > bond pair - bond pair.

Statement II: In a water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)) molecule, the presence of two lone pairs on the central oxygen atom reduces the \(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond angle below the ideal tetrahedral angle of \(109.5^\circ\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory establishes the spatial arrangement of electron pairs around a central atom based on minimizing electrostatic repulsions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is correct because lone pairs are localized solely on the central atom and occupy more space, creating stronger repulsions than shared bonding pairs, which gives the repulsive order: lone pair - lone pair > lone pair - bond pair > bond pair - bond pair.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is correct because oxygen in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) has two lone pairs and two bond pairs; the strong lone pair - lone pair and lone pair - bond pair repulsions push the two \(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bonding pairs closer together, compressing the bond angle to \(104.5^\circ\), which is below \(109.5^\circ\).

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Both statements correctly describe the VSEPR repulsive hierarchy and its direct structural consequence on the geometry of water.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q06 - Properties of canonical forms and resonance hybrid

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a resonance hybrid, the molecule oscillates rapidly back and forth between different canonical structures so that it exists in each form for a definite fraction of time.

Statement II: The resonance hybrid always possesses higher energy and lower stability than any of the individual canonical structures contributing to it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Resonance describes a single unchanging electronic structure represented as a hybrid of multiple canonical Lewis structures; canonical forms have no real independent existence.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is incorrect because the molecule does not oscillate or switch between canonical structures; canonical structures are imaginary constructs and the actual molecule exists as a single stable resonance hybrid at all times.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is incorrect because resonance stabilizes the molecule, meaning the resonance hybrid has lower energy and higher stability than any of the hypothetical contributing canonical structures.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Both statements express common misconceptions regarding resonance by treating canonical structures as dynamic physical states and misstating the energy relationship of the hybrid.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q07 - Molecular orbital energies and magnetism of carbon

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For homonuclear diatomic molecules of the second period with \(Z \le 7\) such as \(\mathrm{B}_2\), \(\mathrm{C}_2\), and \(\mathrm{N}_2\), the \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) molecular orbitals are lower in energy than the \(\sigma 2p_z\) molecular orbital.

Statement II: Diatomic carbon (\(\mathrm{C}_2\)) is paramagnetic because it contains two unpaired electrons in its highest occupied molecular orbitals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Molecular Orbital Theory, the energy level sequence of molecular orbitals for diatomic molecules up to nitrogen (\(Z \le 7\)) is modified by \(2s-2p\) orbital mixing, shifting \(\sigma 2p_z\) above \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is correct because due to \(s-p\) mixing in molecules like \(\mathrm{B}_2\), \(\mathrm{C}_2\), and \(\mathrm{N}_2\), the degenerate \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) orbitals are filled before the \(\sigma 2p_z\) orbital.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is incorrect because \(\mathrm{C}_2\) has \(12\) electrons with the configuration \(\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^* 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^* 2s^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2)\); all electrons are completely paired, which makes \(\mathrm{C}_2\) diamagnetic rather than paramagnetic.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Statement I correctly identifies the orbital energy inversion for lighter diatomics, while Statement II fails because the electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{C}_2\) results in diamagnetism.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Final Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_BONDING_AND_MOLECULAR_STRUCTURE_STMT_Q08 - Axial and equatorial bonds in phosphorus pentachloride

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In phosphorus pentachloride (\(\mathrm{PCl}_5\)) in the gas phase, all five \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds are equal in length and bond dissociation energy.

Statement II: The axial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bond pairs in \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) experience greater repulsive interaction from equatorial bond pairs than equatorial pairs experience among themselves.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The trigonal bipyramidal geometry of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) consists of three equatorial bonds in one plane forming \(120^\circ\) angles with each other, and two axial bonds along the vertical axis forming \(90^\circ\) angles with the equatorial bonds.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Statement I is incorrect because the five \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds are not identical; the two axial bonds are longer (\(240\text{ pm}\)) and weaker than the three equatorial bonds (\(202\text{ pm}\)).

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Statement II is correct because each axial bond pair experiences three strong \(90^\circ\) repulsions from equatorial bond pairs, whereas each equatorial bond pair experiences only two \(90^\circ\) repulsions and two \(120^\circ\) repulsions; the greater repulsion forces the axial bonds to be longer and more vulnerable to cleavage.

Step 4: Comparative Synthesis
Statement I incorrectly claims structural equality for non-equivalent bonds in a trigonal bipyramidal molecule, while Statement II correctly explains the origin of this asymmetry through differential electron pair repulsion.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
